actions.reason: RegexTokenizer._encode_ordinary now encodes all distinct uncached chunks of a call in one batch. It joins them as latin-1 code-point strings with a separator that is in no merge pair (chr(max(inf,256))), then applies the merges in rank order with str.replace, the same as _apply_merges_str. A set of tokens present in the string skips merges that cannot apply. Results are cached per chunk as before. This is only used when the merge preconditions hold (unique int ranks above their pair tokens, below 0x110000) and _encode_chunk is not overridden, so GPT4Tokenizer with its byte shuffle keeps the old path. Outputs are byte-identical and encode_ir drops by 2.9%.
